Description:
AgriYogi bridges the gap between biotechnology and actionable soil intelligence.

We develop biodegradable bio-assay sensors to monitor real-time biological activity in soils, composts, and controlled growing substrates.

Modern cultivation faces a critical challenge: the hidden uncertainty of biological inputs. Growers currently lack real-time verification of whether biofertilizers and biostimulants are active once applied.

AgriYogi creates a live soil data layer that reveals how biology responds under real-use conditions, starting with high-precision environments such as indoor plants and smart greenhouses.

Our platform enables growers to:

Validate biological activity and confirm inputs are functioning

Optimize nutrient and biostimulant use based on real-time soil performance

Prepare for scale by refining precision soil intelligence for open-field and large-scale agriculture

We believe the future of agriculture depends on making the invisible visible, giving growers the confidence to trust biology and unlock its full potential.

Name: VYASN
Description:
VYASN is a marine technology startup based in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, building AI-driven infrastructure for the future of seaweed farming.

Today, seaweed cultivation is largely unmonitored—farmers operate with little visibility into ocean conditions, resulting in inconsistent yields, crop losses, and inefficiencies. VYASN is solving this by deploying AI + IoT-powered smart buoys that capture real-time ocean data, including pH, temperature, salinity, and nutrient levels.

Our platform transforms this data into predictive insights, enabling optimal site selection, early risk detection, and precision farming decisions. By bringing intelligence to the ocean, we aim to make seaweed farming more reliable, scalable, and economically viable.

Built from the Andaman ecosystem and backed by researchers from NIOT, IIT Delhi, IIT Ropar, and JNRM, VYASN operates at the intersection of marine science, AI, and climate technology.

Our mission is to power the next generation of ocean-based agriculture and position India as a global leader in the blue economy.
Location: Port Blair, Andaman And Nicobar Islands, India

Description:
Using existing waste to prevent future waste through our all-natural protective layer that prevents fresh produce from going bad and reduce the colossal waste.

Greenskn is a focused dedicated startup (with experience in Food & Agriculture, at the grassroots level and the end consumer) that is looking to solve this humongous challenge of food waste, one small step at a time. We call ourselves a waste prevention company that follows the circular nature, using waste to prevent waste. The ideal solution would kill the food waste at the source, however, that requires multiple level interventions with multiple stakeholders. Hence in the meantime, we are making use of the current waste to prevent future waste. The next best alternative, till we tackle the problem at its root.

Food loss & waste is a global issue, wherein 1/3 of the world’s food is lost or wasted every year (FAO 2019) amounting to 1.3 Billion Tons of wastage costing the globe $2.6 trillion every year. Not to mention the adverse impact on the environment due to this loss and waste. 

At the environmental impact level, such levels of Food waste consumes;
21% of freshwater
19% of fertilizers
18% of cropland
21% of landfill

Closer home in India, our horticultural sector is characterized by low productivity, high cost of production, significant post-harvest losses, lack of cold chains, and inefficient supply chain leading to the waste of about 30-40% of the fruit and vegetable production.

- 67mn tonnes valued at 92k cr - enough to feed the state of Bihar for a year.
- 520 million tonnes of food was lost in storage and handling while an estimated 780 million tonnes as lost during handling and processing.
- We waste as much food as the whole of the United Kingdom consumes.
- Post-harvest losses of some fresh produce are: 29% of banana, 52% of cauliflower, 38% of mango, and 46% of tomato.

In 1886 on the 30 th of July , a girl was born in a middle class family in a state called �Pudukottai�. She was named Muthulakshmi. One hardly realized that she was Gods creation who would rise in this world to fight Cancer.

This incident sparked of her involvement in cancer and she proposed to build a cancer hospital in Madras. She formed a Cancer relief fund in 1949 and with the support of the WIA she established the cancer hospital in 1954 in a small hut.
She made sure her son, Dr.Krishnamurthy , after completing his medicine in the US stay back in India and serve the cause of poor cancer patients. The rest is now seen in the form of one of the best state  of art Cancer hospitals in the world today.

Astraphage Innovations Pvt. Ltd. is a biotechnology startup building next-generation bacteriophage-based solutions to combat the growing crisis of antimicrobial resistance (AMR).

We are leveraging advances in microbial genomics, bioinformatics, and synthetic biology to develop targeted phage therapeutics and diagnostics tailored to real-world use cases in India.

Our approach is rooted in the One Health framework, addressing AMR across these interconnected sectors:

Human Health: Precision therapeutics and rapid diagnostics for drug-resistant infections such as Diabetic Foot Ulcers and Urinary Tract Infections 
Veterinary Medicine: Phage-based interventions for livestock diseases such as Bovine Mastitis, colibacillosis and salmonellosis to reduce antibiotic overuse
Food Safety & Environment: Biocontrol strategies to limit pathogen spread across supply chains

Astraphage is currently developing an integrated platform that combines phage discovery, genomic characterization, AI-driven host prediction, and translational product development. Our goal is to create deployable, evidence-based solutions that can be integrated into healthcare systems, farms, and food production ecosystems.

By bridging cutting-edge science with practical implementation, we aim to position India at the forefront of the global phage biotechnology revolution, while contributing meaningfully to the fight against antimicrobial resistance.

Description:
“A correct diagnosis is three-fourths the remedy.”
					---Mahatma Gandhi

Rapid and accurate diagnosis is imperative to any medical condition and is instrumental for healthcare professional to make definitivedecision about disease severity and drug dosage. Misdiagnosis and untimely diagnosismay lead to incorrect medications and denial of effective treatment plan, both of which can be potentially toxic to patient’s health. 

We at BioAptagen Laboratories believe that correct diagnosis available at right time and right place can provide an ailing patient a gift of life.

Aptamers have emerged as potential rivals to antibodies in recent decades given their several merits including low production cost, high stability and no limitations on their targets. We are developing diagnostic kits using evolved DNA and peptide Aptamers which can detect and bind pathogens/surface proteins/disease cells in biological fluids.

Why Aptamers over antibodies?

Given their merits over existing conventional drug therapies, Aptamerbased strategieshave found tremendous applications in diagnostics, therapy and drug delivery.

We generate DNA and peptide Aptamers using two well-established techniques, SELEX (Selective Evolution of Ligands by Exponential Enrichment) and Phage Display Technology (Biopanning) respectively. Presently we use bacterial pathogens as our targets for evolution of Aptamers. Aptamers have definitely several merits over existing conventional antibody based diagnostics:

•	Aptamers generated by either by cell-SELEX or biopanning, do not require any prior knowledge of theprotein targets on cell surface facilitating the development of aptamer-guided diagnostics.
•	Aptamers are highly specific and bind to their target with high affinity.
•	Aptamers are thermodynamically stable and unlike antibodies, theyare stable at room temperature.
Product Pipeline

(A)	DNA/Peptide Aptamer based UTI detection kit
(B)	Modified probiotic drink for clearance of gut pathogens

Name: CalciomicsGroup@RCB
Description:
Calcium ions (Ca2+) are tiny but mighty — acting as one of the body's most important signaling molecules, helping cells decide when to grow, divide, and die. Our lab is passionate about understanding how calcium signals work, and using that knowledge to help fight disease.

Why Calcium?
Every cell depends on carefully balanced calcium levels to stay healthy. Calcium moves in and out of tiny compartments inside the cell — like the mitochondria and endoplasmic reticulum — helping cells manage energy, make proteins, and respond to stress. When this balance breaks down, it can contribute to serious conditions including cancer, neurological disorders, and metabolic diseases.

What We Study
Our research sits at the crossroads of calcium biology, skin pigmentation disorders, and cancer. The cells that give skin its color (melanocytes) are highly sensitive to calcium signals — and when those signals go wrong, conditions like vitiligo or abnormal pigmentation develop. We also study how cancer cells hijack calcium signaling to grow, survive, and spread.

Our work focuses on three goals:
 Delineating Organellar Ca2+ Dynamics  — Using advanced imaging tools to watch calcium move inside living cells in real time, revealing how different parts of the cell communicate.
 Elucidating Molecular Mechanisms  — Identifying exactly which proteins and genes are responsible when calcium signaling fails, and how that drives disease.
 Driving Therapeutic Translation  — Translating our findings into new therapies and tools that help better identify and treat patients.

Our Vision
We believe calcium signaling is a largely untapped area with enormous potential. Our mission is to connect lab discoveries to real benefits for patients living with cancer and skin disorders.

Generative Molecule Design
Varentra’s proprietary generative models design and optimize thousands of novel small molecules in silico, efficiently exploring chemical space that is inaccessible to traditional screening and human-driven approaches.

Closed-Loop AI Discovery Engine
We automate the full design → make → test → learn cycle by tightly integrating AI-driven molecular design with automated synthesis and experimental validation. Real-world data continuously retrains our models, compounding performance gains over time.

Precision Target Prioritization
By applying predictive analytics across genomics, clinical, and molecular datasets, Varentra identifies high-value targets earlier—shifting failure upstream, improving capital efficiency, and enabling partners to focus on programs with the highest likelihood of success.

Why Varentra Wins
• Faster progression from target to optimized lead
• Lower discovery costs through automation and AI-driven prioritization
• Higher probability of success via data-reinforced decision making
• Scalable platform applicable across multiple therapeutic areas

The Opportunity
Drug discovery remains slow, expensive, and failure-prone. Varentra’s AI-first approach fundamentally changes the economics of early-stage R&D—enabling faster iteration, deeper chemical exploration, and better decisions at every step.

Description:
We are actively involved in identification and subsequent analysis of important bio-molecular interactions involving proteins, DNA and other macro-molecules in systemic diseases like Cancer and Infectious diseases, like malaria, leishmaniasis, etc. Primary objectives and/or contributions of our research group are to develop robust and efficient approaches to understand the hidden properties of protein-protein interactions (PPI) systems leading to infection/systemic disease by a) integrating large scale “multi-omics” data through network biology/graph theoretical algorithms, mathematical modelling and machine learning techniques, b) in-depth analysis of molecular interaction patterns using state-of-the-art molecular modeling, docking and dynamics strategies, and c) experimental characterization/verification of the identified bio-markers and/or therapeutic targets.
We utilize large-scale genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics data to construct disease or context specific bio-molecular interaction networks and further study them to understand and decipher their biological significance using meta-interactome analysis. Our group also develops various computational tools, techniques and web servers, which are freely available for users and are beneficial to the scientific community throughout the world.
Recently, we have also ventured into developing image processing and machine learning/deep learning based software packages to process and analyze brain MRI and CT images for detection of early features of Alzheimer’s disease and stroke, respectively.

Name: KaviKrishna Laboratory
Description:
KaviKrishna Lab is a not for profit SIRO certified research organisation focusing on Stem Cell Altruism Research. The idea of stem cell altruism is based on Vedic philosophy of AvatarVada Theory; like the individuals cells also reprogram to a Avatar (more powerful) cell when there is any stress or infection in the body either triggered by pathogens or cancer cells. These Avatar Cells or Reprogrammed cells are called Altruistic Stem Cells which activate a stem cell niche defense mechanism to protect their niche from stress. We are trying to develop therapeutics and diagnostics against cancer and TB utilising the mechanism of stem cell niche defense.

The altruistic stem cells were reported by Dr. Bikul Das in embryonic stem cell population in the year 2012. This lab for the first time reported that TB bacteria remain dormant inside bone marrow Mesenchymal Stem Cells (BM-MSCs) even after successful anti-TB treatment for decades (Das B et al, Science Translational Medicine, 2013). This lab also showed how cancer stem cell exploit this altruistic property of stem cell to maintain an asymmetric self renewal for generations (Das B et al, Cancer Research, 2019). Recently this lab showed that coronavirus infection may activate this altruistic stem cell niche defense mechanism in lung MSCs, thus may reactivate the dormant TB bacteria residing in the MSCs (Pathak L et al, American Journal of Pathology, 2021).

The Lab is providing research training program on cancer cell culture, TB bacteria culture and its interaction with stem cell to the graduate and post graduate biotech/life science/microbiology students of north East India.

Four students have completed PhD from the lab and 5 are undergoing PhD in the Lab registered at Gauhati Un diversity and IIT Guwahati. The lab has collaboration with BBCI, Guwahati, IIT Guwahati, JNU, Delhi, Amity University, Noida and with its sister laboratory "Thoreau Laboratory for Global Health, UMass, Lowell, MA, USA".

PathCrisp - A molecular diagnostics platform delivering high-accuracy detection of pathogens and resistance markers, with support for customizable assay design across human, animal, and environmental samples.

EdiCrisp - An end-to-end genome engineering platform offering guide RNA design, custom editing workflows, and creation of engineered cell and organism models, enabling breakthroughs across research and therapeutic development.

CurieCrisp - A preclinical testing and therapeutics development platform built around the N-of-1 strategy, designed to accelerate personalized gene-editing interventions for patients with ultra-rare genetic disorders.

Powered by these platforms, we deliver CRISPR-based products and services across sectors including human health, biomedical research, animal health, food safety, agriculture, sustainability and climate, industrial biotechnology, biosecurity, and biodefense.

At CrisprBits, we are building the tools to rewrite what is possible – for science, for society, and for the future of our planet.

Since its inception, IITMBI has incubated 24 startups with a combined valuation of Rs 281 Cr, cumulative revenue of Rs 5.5 Cr in FY 2022-23, created over 100 direct jobs, and filed 15+ patents. 

IITMBI excels in translating lab-based discoveries into marketable products, nurturing innovation, and bio-entrepreneurship. It promotes collaboration between startups, industry, faculty, and students of IITM. The incubator provides a comprehensive support system for the entrepreneurial journey from idea to market, with dual strategic goals: (a) offering infrastructure for technology scale-up and pilot-scale validation, and (b) fostering research networking for industry-academia collaboration through technical mentorship, business mentoring, funding, and identifying early customers.

Our Mission and Values
Biotron Healthcare’s mission is to equip laboratories with reliable, innovative tools and strong application support – helping teams turn scientific ideas into real-world healthcare impact. We value technical excellence, long-term partnerships, and responsive service, backed by deep domain expertise and hands-on implementation support across research, diagnostics, and manufacturing.

•	Exploration and conservation of microbial diversity of Himachal Pradesh.

•	Promotion of Entrepreneurial skills in multidisciplinary areas of Biotechnology for innovative and R&D and Business activities.

Welcome to Insectika! 

Insectika harnesses the power of insects to combat global warming and improve food security.
Humans are destroying our world in our pursuit to feed the increasing appetite for proteins. We are cutting down forests, emptying the oceans of fish and occupying natural habitats to make farm space to supply nutritious protein to the ever-growing population. Yet, at the same breath, more than a third of all the food we grow goes to waste!

Insectika uses insect farming to recycle ‘green’ and ‘wet’ waste into protein for animal feed. In nature, insects love to feed on rubbish, chicken and fish love eating insects, and humans love eating fish & chickens. Insectika is enhancing these natural processes to industrial-scale insect farming using innovation and technology. With a combination of hardware, software, innovative techniques and a revolutionary business model, we can recycle vast quantities of waste into many tons of insect larvae which can be used economically as fish and poultry feed. By recycling ‘wet’ waste, we reduce the incentive for unsustainable fishing and deforestation, shorten supply chains and reduce greenhouse emissions.

Insectika is helping to c̲l̲e̲a̲n̲ the streets through innovative recycling technologies, f̲e̲e̲d̲ more people by converting waste to protein and s̲a̲v̲e̲ nature by reducing agriculture-induced environmental harm.

Name: Bioremax Innovation Private Limited
Description:
Bioremax Innovation Private Limited (BIPL) is a DPIIT-recognized start up under the Start-up India Initiative and a Udyam-registered Micro and Small Enterprise (MSE), incorporated on 18 July 2024. The company is dedicated to developing environmentally sustainable, science-driven green technologies for environmental remediation and industrial waste management through innovative enzyme-based solutions.
BIPL's flagship innovation is the development of a proprietary enzyme cocktail, BIOREMAX ECODIGESTASETM, derived from naturally occurring microorganisms. BIOREMAX ECODIGESTASETM, can degrade Total Petroleum Hydrocarbons (TPH) at faster rate as compared to live oil degrading bacteria. This breakthrough technology enables rapid, efficient, and eco-friendly bioremediation of oil-contaminated environments, including oily sludge, chemical sludge, crude oil-contaminated soil, oil spill sites on land and water, oil-based drill cuttings, oily waste materials, and hydrocarbon-contaminated wastewater in drains and Nalas.
Unlike conventional microbial based bioremediation technologies, BIOREMAX ECODIGESTASETM quickly catalyses the degradation of complex petroleum hydrocarbons into environmentally benign end products such as fatty acids and water. The enzyme-based process is 100% eco-friendly, non-pathogenic, sustainable, and cost-effective, significantly reducing remediation time while minimizing environmental impact and supporting circular waste management practices.
The development of BIOREMAX ECODIGESTASETM was financially supported by the Central Institute of Petrochemicals Engineering & Technology (CIPET), Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, Government of India, under the Start-up Seed Funding Programme, CIPET provided laboratory facility at their Incubation Centre for research and development of the enzyme based bioremediation solution which  provides safe, efficient, and scalable remediation solutions for operational areas of oil exploration, and petroleum refining

Description:
An estimated 4,000 children die each day from water related diseases, the primary cause being contaminated drinking water. Almost a billion people collect water from open water bodies. These sources are extremely prone to both microbiological and chemical pollution, like cholera, pesticide and industrial pollutants.

Our innovation is a scalable, low tech, activated charcoal producing unit that runs on solar energy. The unit delivers high grade activated charcoal which can be readily incorporated into a slow sand or similar filter to greatly enhance water purification standards.

Our idea stands apart from other clean drinking water solutions because we use existing natural water sources as opposed to drilling for water underground and further tapping strained groundwater resources. Most water filtration solutions rely on single use filters which must be replaced frequently to ensure proper function. Replacing filters is not only environmentally wasteful and financially burdensome but rural communities often do not have ready access to replacements due to their location. The result is communities being forced to drink harmful water.

We address this problem by placing the power to create filters in the hands of the people who use them. Our device is capable of producing a kilogram of activated carbon daily, enough to filter up to 20,000 litres of water. Communities and individuals can be economically empowered through activated carbon and filter production. Conventionally activated carbon is produced in large unsustainable fossil fuel powered industrial furnaces. We use solar power thereby providing a sustainable alternative to polluting methods.

Our Areas of Expertise
1. Genomics - Whole-genome and exome sequencing analysis, variant calling, CNVs, SNPs, and structural variation detection.
2. Transcriptomics - RNA-Seq processing, differential gene expression, gene co-expression networks, and isoform analysis.
3. Epigenomics - DNA methylation, histone modification, and chromatin accessibility analysis.
4. Proteomics & Metabolomics - Mass-spec data processing, protein identification, metabolite profiling, and biomarker discovery.
5. Microbiome & Metagenomics - 16S/18S rRNA, ITS, and shotgun metagenomic analysis for taxonomic and functional profiling.
6. Single-cell Omics - Single-cell RNA-Seq, ATAC-Seq, and data integration using Seurat, Scanpy, and Monocle.
7. Systems Biology & Network Analysis - Integrative modeling, pathway analysis, and regulatory network construction.
What Makes Us Unique
End-to-End Solutions: From consultation to publication, we manage the full spectrum of bioinformatics workflows.
Multi-Omics Integration: Unlock cross-dimensional insights by combining data across different omics platforms.
Custom Pipelines: Bespoke analysis workflows designed using Python, R, and workflow management tools.

We are a computational biology and bioinformatics solutions provider focused on transforming complex biological data into meaningful, research-ready insights. Our work bridges the gap between wet lab experimentation and advanced computational analysis, enabling faster, more accurate scientific discovery.

We specialize in protein and genomic data analysis, including clustering, sequence alignment, structural prediction, and data-driven drug discovery workflows. By leveraging scalable computational pipelines and modern algorithms, we help research teams extract maximum value from their datasets.

Our Mission
To accelerate biological discovery by delivering precise, efficient, and accessible computational analysis.

Name: Ampligene India
Description:
AmpliGene India Biotech is a research-driven biotechnology company focused on advancing next-generation molecular diagnostics through its proprietary AmpEZ technology platform. Our mission is to make molecular testing faster, simpler, and more accessible by enabling a seamless bench-to-site approach that reduces complexity, biosafety requirements, and infrastructure costs.

We develop innovative solutions based on isothermal amplification and smart point-of-care (POCT) systems, empowering users to perform reliable, rapid, and cost-effective testing, even in resource-limited and non-laboratory settings.

Our technology supports a wide range of applications across clinical diagnostics, plant health, GMO testing, veterinary and aquaculture sectors, as well as food and environmental testing. By combining advanced molecular science with user-centric design, we aim to standardize diagnostics while expanding accessibility across diverse industries.

At AmpliGene, we are committed to transforming how diagnostics are delivered- bringing high-quality molecular solutions closer to where they are needed most, and addressing critical global health and biosurveillance challenges with speed, precision, and scalability.

Name: SenViz Labs
Description:
SenViz Labs is a specialized computational consultancy providing high-fidelity data visualization and biostatistical architecture for global genomic research. Founded at IIT Guwahati, we bridge the critical gap between complex raw datasets and publication-ready scientific narratives.

Our core expertise lies in the intersection of Population Genetics and Biocomputation. We understand that for high-impact research, "good enough" visualization is not enough. We deliver 600 DPI, journal-standard Manhattan plots, QQ plots, and Circos diagrams that meet the rigorous requirements of Q1 publications and investor pitch decks.

Our Specialized Solutions:

    GWAS Visualization: Custom, high-resolution plotting with precise loci labeling and color mapping.

    Biostatistical Architecture: Rigorous data cleaning and statistical validation for genomic cohorts.

    Technical Deck Design: "Scientifically tight" presentation decks for conferences, PIs, and venture capital.

    Deep-Tech Research Support: Expertise in medical genetics, specifically focusing on the Indian Population (including Biliary Atresia susceptibility).

At SenViz Labs, we take the computational burden off your research team so you can focus strictly on the biology. Whether you are a university lab preparing for a submission or a biotech startup seeking to visualize your IP, we provide the technical clarity your data deserves.

LC Process, team of professionals in India and around the globe, involved in various technique of Chromatography. The technology that has endless applications from analytical chromatography, preparative to plant scale chromatography. Further classified into low pressure, medium and high pressure chromatography, HPLC still remain the most popular among these. Open column is the base of chromatography technique, where the column is filled with silica and solvent flow through gravity poured from top of the column, separating the compound, the fractions are collected at the bottom of the column. Open column chromatography was further improved and developed into a set of instrumentation, now known as HPLC, MPLC, LPLC, Flash etc. by combining pumps, detectors and column. Chromatography is considered amongst the most accurate technique of analytical measurement of components in a mixture. Name: Apratima Biosolutions
Description:
Planet earth has more plastic waste (around 4900 Mt or million metric tons), than the total mass of the animal kingdom ~2589 Mt! The most common method of recycling plastic is by mechanical process followed by chemical or thermal. In the mechanical process, plastic waste is either converted to other articles of downgraded quality or downcycled to polyester for the textile industry. Other methods require use of either chemicals or high temperatures. Manufacturing of plastic itself contributes to the pollution, it is estimated that 4% of global oil is used for plastic production.
It is impossible for human civilization to completely stop using or even to reduce plastic usage. Therefore it is more important we have an efficient close-loop recycling system which can put the plastic back for commercial use without compromising on the quality of the recycled product at the same time not polluting the environment and simultaneously reducing or completely eliminating the need to derive them from crude oil. The most popular existing technologies can only satisfy a maximum of two of these constraints.
One such effort is under process at "Apratima Biosolutions" wherein we are devising an eco-friendly, energy efficient, low carbon footprint technology to degrade plastic waste into its building blocks, which can again be used to make new virgin quality polymer. We use powerful tools provided by Mother nature and AI! This is our first step towards the ultimate solution to make our environment free from plastic or other pollutants, and create a healthy and safe environment for life on the planet.

Description:
Avesthagen Limited - Brief Summary

Avesthagen is a leading systems biology life science company uniquely positioned to help solve some of the world’s biggest healthcare and environmental challenges. Since its inception 20 years ago, Avesthagen has introduced new ideas, technologies, and products, for the life sciences market. 
The Avestagenome Project is Avesthagen’s largest epidemiological study ever conducted in India, and the first such detailed system biology study worldwide on an endogamous population. The project has collected a biobank of Parsi blood samples with extensive patient data from 4,500 members and investigates the molecular basis of longevity and age-related disorders, prioritizing cancers, cardiovascular disease, diabetes and neurological disorders.
Recognizing the importance of the Parsi cohort and the unique systems’ biology approach to research, the U.S.-based Foundation for a Smoke-Free World, whose mission is to end smoking within this generation, recently awarded a grant to Avesthagen Limited to prioritize research into lung and tobacco-related cancers. Avesthagen will combine liquid biopsy, next-generation sequencing (NGS), state- of-the-art bioinformatics, artificial intelligence and machine learning to identify predictive and early-stage biomarkers of cancers in smokers. The project will use non-Parsi smoker and non-smoker samples from the wider Indian and other populations to gain further insights into the evidence behind such data. 
Avesthagen is expected to be a key player in the lucrative personalised medicine market, which is projected to reach a value of US $1.7 trillion by 2026. 

Today, Avesthagen is proud to build on this heritage by partnering with others to tackle unprecedented challenges now facing our world. We believe we can provide enough healthy food for people everywhere and protect the environment for generations to come.

Name: Sanzyme Biologics
Description:
Sanzyme Biologics is a pioneering leader in the field of probiotics and fermentation-derived nutritional ingredients. Established in 1969 as Uni-Sankyo, a joint venture with Sankyo, Japan, we were the first company in India to manufacture and sell probiotics and enzymes. Over the decades, we've evolved into a global powerhouse, specializing in shelf-stable, spore-forming probiotic strains and fermentation-derived products.

Our Expertise:
Probiotic Strains: We offer a diverse portfolio of well-researched, effective, and safe probiotic strains, including Bacillus coagulans SNZ 1969, Bacillus subtilis SNZ 1972TM, Bacillus clausii SNZ 1971TM, and Saccharomyces boulardii SNZ 1986TM. These strains are widely used in food, dietary supplements, pharmaceuticals, aquaculture, poultry, pet food, and agriculture applications.

Fermentation Technology: With over 50 years of experience, we have honed our fermentation technology to produce high-quality probiotics and enzymes, ensuring consistency and safety in every batch.

Global Reach: Our products are trusted by customers in over 40 countries, including the United States, Europe, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand, China, and Taiwan.

Manufacturing Excellence: State-of-the-Art Facilities: We operate two independent manufacturing facilities in Hyderabad, India, with a combined fermentation capacity exceeding 350,000 liters, making us one of the largest producers of probiotics globally.

Certifications: Our facilities are NSF certified and adhere to global standards, including ISO 22000, ISO 14000, ISO 9000, GMP, Halal, Kosher, and non-GMO certifications.

Our Commitment: At Sanzyme Biologics, we are dedicated to advancing human and animal health through innovative probiotic solutions. Our team of over 300 professionals works tirelessly to develop science-backed products that enhance the quality of life.

Name: Institute of Advanced Virology
Description:
Institute of Advanced Virology (IAV) is an autonomous institution under Science & Technology, Govt. of Kerala focusing research, diagnosis and management of emerging and re-emerging infectious viral diseases. The Advanced Molecular Diagnostic Facility (AMDF) of IAV has the capacity to diagnose  80+ viral pathogens including Nipah & KFD. AMDF functions as the referral diagnostic facility for tertiary level  hospitals in Kerala.
IAV is in the process of establishing a BSL III facility and a Small Animal Experimental Facility; and the same is expected to be operational in a period of one year.
 IAV facilitates for dissertation/internship for graduate and PG students in life sciences and short term hands on training programmes so as to create a talented and trained pool of manpower in various domains of Virology.

Name: Bhami's Research Laboratory (BRL)
Description:
Established in the year 2014, BRL is the brain-child of highly experienced scientists and entrepreneurs in biopharma industry. 

Biologic therapies, especially monoclonal antibodies(mAbs) have transformed modern medicine. However, many of these therapies are still administered through intravenous (IV) infusion, creating challenges around patient convenience, healthcare infrastructure, and overall treatment cost.

At Bhami’s Research Labs (BRL), we are addressing this gap through our proprietary BRLSubQ Platform technology, a formulation designed to enable the transition IV to SubQ.

BRLSubQ focuses on one of the most critical barriers in SubQ biologics: Increased viscosity at high concentrations. As mAbs are concentrated to enable low-volume injections, viscosity increases significantly, making administration difficult or even impractical. Our platform is engineered to overcome this limitation by enabling high-concentration formulations (225–250 mg/mL) while maintaining low viscosity (~20 cP)—a combination that is essential for viable SubQ delivery.

This capability opens up new possibilities for both innovator biologics and biosimilars:

- Conversion of IV therapies into patient-friendly SubQ injections
- Reduction in administration time and dependence on infusion centers
- Potential for improved patient compliance and accessibility

Name: Evolutionary Venomics Lab
Description:
In the Evolutionary Venomics Lab at the Centre for Ecological Sciences (CES), Indian Institute of Science (IISC), we investigate venomous animals and their venoms as model systems to address basic but broad questions in evolutionary biology and genetics. Using state-of-the-art technologies across multiple disciplines, we examine the fascinating evolutionary histories of the enigmatic lineages of venomous animals and their venoms.

A particular emphasis is placed on characterizing the composition, toxicity profiles and evolutionary dynamics of venoms of the ‘big four’ snakes in India, as the lab will strive to deliver advanced antivenom with a commensurate improvement in safety, specificity, and affordability of treatment. The protein composition, and hence the pathogenic potential of venoms, can exhibit dramatic geographical variation, with different populations of the same species having starkly distinct venom profiles and, consequently, resulting in a significantly reduced antivenom efficiency. Therefore, the lab will unravel intra- and interspecific venom variability in medically significant Indian snakes and utilize this information for the molecular design of effective snakebite therapy.

The other broad aims of the lab include (a) investigating genomes, transcriptomes and proteomes of neglected venomous lineages (e.g., scorpions, spiders, centipedes, jellyfish, Hymenoptera, etc.) to understand the molecular basis of venom production, regulation, and evolutionary diversification; (b) understanding the genetic basis of venom resistance in the venomous animal and its prey/predators; (c) unravelling the evolutionary forces that have shaped the current distribution of venomous animals in the Indian subcontinent, and (d) investigating the therapeutic potential of venom proteins.

Our work spans next-generation sequencing (NGS), whole genome and exome analysis, targeted panels, transcriptomics, RNA sequencing, metagenomics, variant interpretation, and integrated multi-layered biological data workflows. We focus on transforming complex genomic and transcriptomic datasets into structured, interpretable, and decision-ready outputs through robust computational pipelines and reproducible analytical systems.

Modern sequencing technologies have dramatically scaled biological data generation. However, extracting meaningful biological signal from high-dimensional datasets remains a major challenge due to technical variability, batch effects, sequencing artifacts, transcript complexity, and inconsistencies across analytical workflows. ATGeneCare addresses these challenges through rigorous quality control, standardized preprocessing, normalization, batch correction, annotation frameworks, and advanced interpretation strategies designed to preserve biological relevance while minimizing technical noise.

Our analytical ecosystem integrates multiple layers of genomic and transcriptomic information, including differential expression profiling, splicing analysis, fusion detection, expression outlier analysis, somatic and germline variant interpretation, pathway-level insights, and clinically relevant annotation workflows. We emphasize scalable, reproducible, and computationally robust systems capable of supporting both exploratory research and clinically actionable interpretation.

At ATGeneCare, bioinformatics is approached as infrastructure for modern biology, enabling the translation of large-scale sequencing data into biological insight, functional understanding, and data-driven decision-making.

Description:
BioVikas is a deep-tech biorefinery converting Indian agricultural residue into high-value molecules.

We make two product families from one process line:

• Functional prebiotics — xylo-oligosaccharides (XOS) for animal feed, food, beverage and nutraceutical use. Effective at 1.4–2.8 g/day against 8–10 g for FOS, which makes XOS the cheapest common prebiotic per effective dose despite a higher price per kilogram.

• Thermostable bio-rheology modifiers — industrial performance materials targeting imported additives in packaging paper, high-strength cement and drilling fluids. Under validation; we are seeking industrial partners to run trials.

Why the economics work: a corn cob is three polymers. The hemicellulose fraction becomes prebiotics and carries the margin. The cellulose and lignin fractions become industrial materials that cover operating cost. The prebiotic doesn't have to carry the plant.

What makes us different:

• Fully indigenous — every process, piece of equipment and person developed in India. Zero imported technology, equipment, process know-how or personnel. All core IP owned outright, no licensing encumbrances.

• Traceable — every batch carries a certification-ready record of energy footprint, water footprint and supply-chain provenance.

• Clean process — food-grade additives only, with no harsh chemical residues requiring downstream removal.

First market: animal and aqua feed. Indian shrimp exports are being rejected for banned antibiotic residues, and those antibiotics exist to manage disease pressure that begins in the gut. Feed-grade XOS needs no human-food clearance, so it is the fastest route from our line to a real problem.

Name: 4baseCare
Description:
Founded in 2018 by Hitesh Goswami and Kshitij Rishi, 4baseCare is a precision oncology company focused on enabling personalized cancer care through genomics. The company develops population-specific genomic insights that help oncologists make more informed, evidence-based treatment decisions for Indian patients. By analysing the genetic profile of a patient's tumour, 4baseCare supports clinicians in identifying therapies that are more likely to be effective, reducing trial-and-error in treatment and improving patient outcomes.

Recognising that much of global precision oncology is built on genomic data from Western populations, 4baseCare has developed solutions tailored to the unique genetic landscape of Indian and Asian patients. Its flagship comprehensive genomic profiling test, TARGTTM Indiegene, provides clinically actionable insights that enable more precise treatment selection.

The company has also developed OncoTwin Insights, an AI-powered clinico-genomic intelligence platform that combines real-world genomic, clinical and outcomes data to support oncologists in making personalized treatment decisions. The platform was recently selected for the prestigious MSK iHub program at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, New York.

Headquartered in Bengaluru, 4baseCare has established one of India's largest precision oncology ecosystems and collaborates with leading hospitals, cancer centres and clinicians across the country. In 2026, the company closed its Series B funding round at ₹128 crore, backed by investors including growX Ventures, Infosys, Yali Capital, Ashish Kacholia and Lashit Sanghvi, to further accelerate innovation and expand access to precision oncology.

Name: Mestastop Solutions
Description:
Cancer can be broken down into four parts; mainly initiation, progression, immunosuppression, and finally metastasis, leading to death. Initiation and progression happen due to genetic reasons along with the interplay of the tumor microenvironment, whereas immunosuppression is the inefficiency of the body’s immune system to recognize and destroy cancer cells. Metastasis is the movement of tumor cells through the blood and the formation of multiple tumors into different secondary sites of the body. Metastasis is responsible for almost 90% of cancer deaths. 

Unfortunately, though cancer treatment has advanced with targeted therapy and immunotherapy, there is still a huge gap as none of them addresses metastasis. One of the main reasons for these are the challenges faced in advancing a molecule targeting metastasis; from suitable In vitro models to the perfect animal model that will closely resemble the biology without alleviating cost and timelines. 

Mestastop aims to provide a solution for such challenges with their unique proprietary platforms, METAssay, METSCAN, and METVivo.

Established in 2009, the young team of scientists at 'Shodhaka' began with the herculean task of compiling, cataloguing and scientifically comparing the existing databases and software. The public web-portal startbioinfo.com - launched in 2010, and some of our publications illustrate our efforts in this direction. We are perhaps the only organization (at least a commercial one) that has spent more than 8 years in systematically comparing several types of such bioinformatic resources. This work has helped us to add value to services to the research projects of our client-scientists. The work not only helped us to determine the right choices among the tools and databases for specific tasks, but also identify gaps in the availability of such resources for certain applications. In such cases, we have been developing required databases and software for public use in collaboration with IBAB (www.ibab.ac.in), an institute that promotes entrepreneurship and where the founder director (Prof. Kshitish Acharya) continues to serve as a faculty scientist.

We have now completed multiple service-projects in the areas of NGS and microarray data analysis. We have also been active in the areas of biocuration, custom-designing databases & software, biomarker discovery by in silico approaches, and assisting scientists in manuscript writing/refining. We excited about the possibility reaching more researchers and contributing to their scientific endeavors. Do contact us please, if you have any bioinformatic or biostatistic need.

• Reactivate beneficial soil microorganisms

Citozeatec represents a research-led approach to enzyme science, emphasizing how specific enzyme substrates function as essential biochemical inputs for cellular activity. Heliozyme brings this globally established scientific framework to India with a focus on precision, transparency, and evidence-based communication, ensuring alignment with international research standards while remaining locally relevant.

Rather than relying on generic wellness narratives, Heliozyme emphasizes a mechanism-driven understanding of enzyme function at the cellular level. Our work is informed by scientific literature, biochemical principles, and responsible formulation practices, with a clear commitment to integrity and long-term credibility.

Heliozyme’s philosophy is rooted in education, scientific clarity, and trust. We aim to engage healthcare professionals, researchers, institutions, and informed stakeholders by presenting enzyme science in a clear, accurate, and accessible manner-without exaggerated claims or oversimplification.

As an emerging contributor to India’s biotechnology and life sciences ecosystem, Heliozyme seeks to collaborate with research institutions, scientific experts, and industry partners who share a commitment to responsible innovation. Our mission is to strengthen the understanding of enzyme science and cellular biology in India, while building a credible, research-aligned platform around Citozeatec for long-term impact.

Heliozyme stands for science that works at the cellular level - grounded in research, guided by integrity, and built for India.

.

 How proteins fold, unfold, and interact under force

 How ligand-receptor pairs recognize and bind with incredible precision

eCRF and EDC Design Automation: Instantly generate CRFs, domain-specific forms, and study data specifications based on CDISC standards.

Metadata Intelligence: Interpret and map biomedical concepts to standardized variables, controlled terminology, and ontology references.

Clinical Data Interoperability: Bridge study design elements across USDM, SDTM, and CDASH models for consistency and traceability.

Scholarly Context Awareness: Provides evidence-based, standards-compliant responses tailored for researchers, data managers, and clinical programmers.

By integrating domain expertise with generative intelligence, CLINVA transforms how clinical data standards and study metadata are managed — enabling faster, smarter, and compliant research execution across the life sciences ecosystem.

Name: A.S.E Analytics LLP
Description:
We perform classification and recognition of complex liquids in the same way as humans do which is very untypical type of analysis for conventional analytical chemistry and traditional analytical techniques. Taste Masking, Benchmarking or Reference Matching.....

Taste, Flavours or odors are so entwined in our experience that most people are unaware that most of what they call taste is really an olfactory experience.

The artificial taste assessment can be a very challenging task when the substances responsible for the taste have different chemical structure. 
To evaluate bitterness of NCE, we generate quantitative prediction of bitterness scores (calibration) of diverse APIs, both inorganic and organic, on the basis of a multivariate calibration based on known (Human) H Scores. Influence of the lipophilicity of the substances on the sensor response may be especially important for the measurements of bitterness intensity as hydrophobicity was reported to be correlated with bitterness intensity. 

Our studies involving ODTs - Oradispersible  tablets demonstrates the influence of the  dissolution medium on the drug release rate at different time points starting 15 seconds. 

Wide spectrum of host of instruments are available which have different active principles having a bias on latest developments of analytical instrumentation. These have to be evaluated and our current level of knowledge of understanding has to be broadened to disseminate the knowledge to the user industry. This serves the twin objectives, of application of state of art technology and serve the interest of consumers who are vulnerable due to subjective evaluation.

Name: INTRINSIC
Description:

New ideas and new tools are coming out every month in journals like Nature Methods and Nature Biotechnology, yet a lot of people do not get the chance to follow these updates. This creates a gap where many talented scientists feel left behind or unsure of how to keep up with modern techniques.

INTRINSIC, the Integrative Translational Research in Systems and Clinical Bioinformatics Consortium, was started to help close this gap. This is a non profit group that wants to make modern bioinformatics clear, approachable, and useful for everyone in the community.

INTRINSIC is a space where students, researchers, and clinicians can learn together and stay updated with the latest technologies. We share and explain new papers from top journals like Nature Methods, Nature Biotechnology, Cell Systems, Bioinformatics, and Genome Research in a simple and practical way.

Here the page focuses on:
• Next generation computational methods
• Modern ML and AI in biology
• Multi omics integration
• Clinical and translational informatics
• New tools, workflows, and pipelines

The main goal is to make sure no one feels left out of the progress happening in science. By helping people understand the newest ideas and practices, INTRINSIC hopes to support and inspire the next generation of computational biologists and translational researchers.

Name: C Y Plastic recycling
Description:
Plastic recycling is the reprocessing of plastic waste into new and useful products. When performed correctly, this can reduce dependence on landfills, conserve resources and protect the environment from plastic pollution and greenhouse gas emissions.
The simplest of plastic recycling processes involves collecting, sorting, shredding, washing, melting, and pelletizing. The actual particular processes vary based on plastic resin or type of plastic product.
The plastic recycling process steps
1. Collection + distribution
The first step in the mechanical recycling process is the collection of post-consumer materials from homes, businesses, and institutions.  This can be done by either local government or private companies, with the latter often a popular option for businesses.

Another option is taking plastics to communal collection points such as designated recycling bins or facilities. This may be as simple as a bottle bank on a street corner or as complex as a local waste site with large areas for various recyclable and non-recyclable municipal solid waste (MSW).

2. Sorting + categorizing
The next step in the plastic recycling process is sorting. There are several different types of plastic (see below), which need to be separated from each other by recyclers. Further to that, plastics might be sorted by other properties such as color, thickness, and use. This is done by machines at the recycling plant and is an important step to increase the efficiency of plants and avoid the contamination of end products.

3. Washing
Washing is a crucial step in the plastic recycling process since it removes some of the impurities that can impede the operation, or completely ruin a batch of recycled plastic. The impurities targeted in this step commonly include things such as product labels and adhesives as well as dirt and food residue. Name: Beacon OS
Description:
BeaconOS is an IND readiness platform for modern biotech teams.

Today's biotech stack was never designed to answer a simple question:

"Are we actually ready for IND, and what should happen next?"

Discovery platforms help design therapies. Laboratory systems manage experimental data. Consultants provide point-in-time assessments. Regulatory operations platforms manage submissions.

But biotech teams are still left stitching together spreadsheets, emails, reports, and expert opinions to understand what regulators will expect, what evidence is missing, and how close a program is to IND readiness.

BeaconOS fills that gap.

We help organizations understand what regulators are likely to expect, identify evidence gaps, and operationalize the path from therapeutic candidate to IND preparation.

BeaconOS transforms fragmented readiness activities into a continuously updated system that connects regulatory expectations, evidence generation, and CMC execution.

What BeaconOS enables:

• Regulatory expectations mapped to therapeutic programs across FDA, ICH, and EMA frameworks
• Requirement-level readiness assessments showing what's missing, why it matters, and recommended next steps
• Evidence tracking linked to the requirements it addresses, creating traceability across teams
• Structured workflows to coordinate experiments, documentation, and readiness activities
• First-pass CMC authoring generated from program data to reduce repetitive work

Built for seed-to-Series B biotech companies, CMC and regulatory leaders, CROs, consultancies, and virtual biotech teams preparing for IND.

BeaconOS complements the systems biotech teams already rely on. It does not replace discovery platforms, laboratory systems, CROs, or regulatory operations software. It helps them work from the same continuously updated understanding of IND readiness.

BeaconOS is a decision-support and operational readiness platform. It does not provide legal or regulatory advice.
